parsed.explanation: High Risk. No trans-specific criminalisation of presentation is documented, and border treatment is unresolved, but the combined regime is hostile if the visitor is outed: the buggery law remains (secondary), there is no gender-identity anti-discrimination or recognition framework, police are documented leaking reports and failing to investigate anti-LGBT violence, social disapproval is extreme, and custody exposes LGBT prisoners to severe violence, isolation and corrective rape. A 2013 mob killing of a gender-nonconforming minor remains unsolved. Local Pride was blocked and police said they could not protect. Tourist-resort insulation and a tourism welcome statement are not enforceable protections. Absence of documented visitor border incidents is not safety.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border, visa or gender-marker screening practice for trans visitors; no legal gender recognition exists, but visitors use home documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Unresolved whether document mismatch would trigger referral or disclosure; absence of evidence is not safety.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Detention exposes to overcrowding, prisoner-on-prisoner anti-LGBT violence, no gender-recognition accommodation framework, isolation and corrective rape; police leak incident details.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No working protection documented; complaints can increase danger.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest under the same-sex statute or public-order detention could place a trans visitor in unspecialised, birth-sex custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prison and hospital staff harassment of LGBT patients/inmates documented; custody conditions are severe and anti-LGBT violence is common.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No specialised housing policy or visitor-facing facility protection documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Custody stage interacts with the absence of any gender-recognition framework for placement decisions.

care_services.exposure: Trans health-care service exclusion documented for residents; no visitor-specific denial documented.
care_services.interaction: Short-term visitor care exposure is not documented, though emergency disclosure could occur.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Buggery law punishable by up to 10 years hard labour; no gender-identity anti-discrimination statute; police harassment of trans women and failure to investigate anti-LGBT violence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No statutory protection; a tourism welcome statement is not enforceable.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Same-sex law is secondary but can become a police lever, especially if travelling with a partner; police response is hostile or indifferent.

minors_guardians.exposure: A gender-nonconforming 16-year-old was mobbed, stabbed and shot dead in 2013; the case remained unsolved as of 2022. No specific protections for trans minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent or guardian has no documented recourse if a trans minor is targeted.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Violence against LGBT people is common and underreported; 2012 raw counts include 68 harassment/abuse reports, 53 assaults and at least two killings; trans women face police harassment.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Tourist resort areas are described as insulated bubbles; this is not a legal protection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Outing can trigger assault, and reporting may expose the victim to police leaks or inaction.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no gender-recognition framework, documented police impunity and failure to investigate; a media-access challenge was rejected.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Complaints are unsafe or ineffective; border treatment remains unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A. Vellandra documents universal border denial and exclusion without imprisonment; this dossier lacks documented routine border exclusion but records lethal anti-trans violence, police impunity, and severe custodial danger if outed.

Broadly similar to 0.25-B. Meridia documents routine extortion and overnight cells; this dossier lacks that specific visitor shakedown evidence but records graver anti-LGBT violence, unsolved mob killing, and unsafe custody, with no functioning remedy.

Higher than 0.15-A. Varnalia criminalises gender presentation and routinely arrests visitors, with months of pretrial custody and beatings; here no explicit presentation offence or routine visitor arrest is documented, though the background is severe.

Lower than 0.45-D. Drellia imposes universal registration exposure but documents no credible lethal punishment; this dossier has less routine state registration but documented anti-trans violence, police failure, and dangerous custody, making the consequences if outed more severe.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a latent same-sex statute with no statutory gender-identity protection and documented police indifference or harassment. The most severe exposure is conditional: if outed and detained, a trans visitor enters unspecialised, birth-sex custody with documented anti-LGBT prisoner violence and no safe complaint route. In public, violence is common and underreported, and police response is unreliable. Local episodes—blocked Pride, police inability to protect, and an unsolved mob killing—corroborate that the state will not reliably protect a visibly trans visitor. Border/document risk is unresolved and not scored as a documented exposure. This is High Risk: not catastrophic state targeting, but well below Reduced Risk.
